diagrams.title: From Borrower File to Retained Brokerage Fee
diagrams.subtitle: Five operating stages; loan principal never enters brokerage revenue.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The brokerage arranges commercial financing rather than funding loans. Revenue consists only of retained origination or referral fees earned under the applicable agreement. First-deal planning remains 3–9 months; stage numbers indicate sequence, not duration.
diagrams.caption: A signed term sheet is neither a closing nor earned cash. Track failed closings and commission-reversal exposure separately.

stages.label: Qualify the mandate
stages.detail: Record borrower jurisdiction, business purpose, financing amount, collateral, and requested timing in HubSpot. Confirm the brokerage can perform the proposed activity before accepting a fee-bearing engagement.

stages.label: Assemble the credit file
stages.detail: Collect financial statements, bank records, debt schedules, equipment invoices or receivables aging, and authorized contact details. Use a restricted document portal rather than forwarding borrower files through shared inboxes.

stages.label: Match the lender matrix
stages.detail: Filter Airtable lender records by geography, ticket size, industry, collateral, leverage, and lender-defined coverage requirements. Record each decline reason and permission to share the file with each selected lender.

stages.label: Coordinate credit and closing
stages.detail: Maintain a closing-condition checklist and reconcile borrower-facing fees with lender agreements. The lender owns underwriting and funding; the broker verifies compensation terms, payor identity, and reversal triggers.

stages.label: Reconcile and service
stages.detail: Match the earned-fee record to the lender settlement statement and bank receipt. Separate contingent amounts, track clawback windows, and schedule renewal outreach without representing loan principal as operator sales.

diagrams.title: Forty Funded Placements Support the Base Case
diagrams.subtitle: One annual borrower cohort; every downstream count is a subset.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Illustrative steady-state annual cohort, not a first-month forecast. Count each financing opportunity once and exclude duplicate lender submissions. Forty funded, fee-retaining placements at $14,000 average retained compensation produce $560,000 operator gross revenue.
diagrams.caption: Stage conversion rates are 60.0%, 50.0%, 53.3%, and 62.5%; overall conversion is 10.0%. The $14,000 fee is a modeled average, not a market quotation.

stages.label: Permissioned opportunities
stages.detail: Source documented borrower introductions through accountants, equipment dealers, and existing relationships. Deduplicate financing requests before measuring acquisition cost or assigning the relationship manager.

stages.label: Qualified financing requests
stages.detail: Retain borrowers whose business purpose, geography, financing size, and timing fit the desk's permitted scope and at least one current lender appetite.

stages.label: Complete lender-ready files
stages.detail: Require current financial evidence, a reconciled debt schedule, appropriate collateral documentation, and authorized distribution before counting a file as complete.

stages.label: Accepted conditional terms
stages.detail: Count borrower-accepted lender terms with remaining closing conditions logged. Do not recognize brokerage fees merely because an indicative offer was issued.

stages.label: Funded and fee-retaining placements
stages.detail: Reconcile 40 placements times $14,000 to $560,000 retained annual fee revenue. Exclude failed closings and amounts reversed or unearned; maintain a separate contingent-compensation exposure register.

diagrams.title: $560,000 Retained Fees to $196,000 Owner Net
diagrams.subtitle: Four expense deductions reconcile exactly to a 35.0% net margin.
diagrams.assumptions_note: All values are annual USD. First and last bars are totals; the four intervening bars are negative expense movements. Cost allocations are illustrative, while revenue, profit, and margin match the canonical Base Case. The published $4,000–$18,000 monthly operating range is not an all-in annual expense ceiling: this model requires $364,000 total annual expenses, averaging $30,333.33 monthly. Do not infer that the published range funds every modeled expense.
diagrams.caption: $560,000 − $156,000 − $60,000 − $84,000 − $64,000 = $196,000; $196,000 / $560,000 = 35.0%. Retained fees exclude loan principal and already reflect fee reversals for the modeled cohort.

stages.label: Retained brokerage revenue
stages.detail: Opening total equals retained origination and referral fees across 40 funded placements. Borrower loan proceeds and lender-funded principal remain outside this revenue bar.

stages.label: Pod delivery compensation
stages.detail: Illustrative compensation and employment-cost envelope for two full-time seats and two part-time contractor seats. Validate local hiring costs and owner compensation treatment before adopting this staffing budget.

stages.label: Recurring operating infrastructure
stages.detail: Budget $5,000 monthly for CRM, secure document handling, insurance, accounting, office services, and baseline professional support. Keep transaction-dependent costs outside this recurring infrastructure subtotal.

stages.label: Acquisition and relationship development
stages.detail: Allocate $2,100 per funded placement across 40 outcomes for industry outreach, events, content, and relationship development. Any compensated referral requires a separate activity, licensing, and fee-permissibility assessment.

stages.label: Transaction and exception handling
stages.detail: Allocate $1,600 per funded outcome across the whole pipeline for specialized file review, transaction counsel, verification, and failed-file work. Exclude costs already charged to staffing, infrastructure, or acquisition.

stages.label: Annual owner net profit
stages.detail: Closing total matches the canonical Base Case after all four expense deductions. Treat this bar as the resulting total rather than an additional positive movement in the waterfall.

diagrams.title: Compare Retained Fees, Not Financed Principal
diagrams.subtitle: Illustrative retained USD per $1,000,000 funded placement.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Each bar uses an identical illustrative $1,000,000 financed amount. Values are retained brokerage fees, not lender yields or quoted market rates. Eight placements in each of five categories produce 40 closings, $40,000,000 underlying principal, and $560,000 operator revenue. Fees require transaction-specific permissibility, agreement, disclosure, and retention.
diagrams.caption: Eight times ($15,000 + $10,000 + $10,000 + $20,000 + $15,000) equals $560,000. The equal-weight average is $14,000 retained fees per funded placement.

stages.label: Equipment acquisition debt
stages.detail: Model eight placements producing $120,000 retained fees. Verify equipment invoices, asset identification, useful life, advance rate, and lien position before sending the collateral package to lenders.

stages.label: Receivables-backed facilities
stages.detail: Model eight placements producing $80,000 retained fees. Review dilution, debtor concentration, eligibility exclusions, and borrowing-base reporting; model no recurring residual compensation unless contractually earned.

stages.label: SBA-backed business loans
stages.detail: Model eight placements producing $80,000 retained fees. This percentage is an arithmetic assumption, not an authorized tariff; apply 13 CFR 103.5, current program requirements, and Form 159 where required.

stages.label: Commercial bridge debt
stages.detail: Model eight placements producing $160,000 retained fees. Verify repayment exit, maturity, collateral valuation, and extension terms; resolve real-estate broker licensing requirements when collateral triggers them.

stages.label: Purchase-order working capital
stages.detail: Model eight placements producing $120,000 retained fees. Confirm purchase-order authenticity, supplier performance, customer acceptance conditions, and control of proceeds before selecting an appropriate funding structure.

diagrams.title: Four Checks Before a Live Financing Submission
diagrams.subtitle: Advance on documented fit; unresolved branches stop the affected activity.
diagrams.assumptions_note: These are sequential checks, not a universal licensing determination. Jurisdiction, collateral, product, compensation, and the broker's actual conduct control applicability. Numeric values identify check order rather than risk scores.
diagrams.caption: Keep the legal-scope record beside the lender matrix. A lender relationship does not itself authorize brokerage activity, fee collection, or securities placement.

stages.label: Activity and licensing
stages.detail: Map borrower, broker, and collateral jurisdictions. California Financial Code Section 22100 requires licensing for covered finance-lender or broker activity, subject to applicable exceptions and scope. Analyze real-estate brokerage separately. Securities activity requires analysis under 15 U.S.C. 78o(a)(1); stop that activity until the required registration path is resolved.

stages.label: Compensation and disclosure
stages.detail: Identify each payor, service, fee amount, earning event, and clawback trigger before engagement. For covered SBA agent services, apply 13 CFR 103.5 and required Form 159 disclosures. Assess state commercial-financing disclosure duties by role and product; revise unsupported or impermissible compensation arrangements before proceeding.

stages.label: Fair lending and file security
stages.detail: Use documented credit-fit criteria under ECOA, 15 U.S.C. 1691, and Regulation B, 12 CFR part 1002. Determine creditor status and allocate notice duties without erasing statutory responsibility. For covered institutions, implement 16 CFR part 314 safeguards; use MFA, restricted access, and documented data handling.

stages.label: Collateral and closing exposure
stages.detail: Confirm who verifies attachment and perfection under UCC 9-203 and 9-310, including applicable exceptions. Check lender concentration, closing conditions, and commission reversal terms. Use an internal 35% single-lender retained-revenue review threshold; excess concentration triggers diversification planning, not a claimed statute.

diagrams.title: Four Core Seats, Two Scale Seats
diagrams.subtitle: Base and Conservative: 2 FT + 2 C; Scaled: 3 FT + 3 C.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Each stage represents one person; contractor seats are part-time engagements, not full-time equivalents. Numeric values represent one person each. First four seats form the core pod; final two are scale additions. Compensation is scenario-specific and must be tested against actual hiring costs.
diagrams.caption: Conservative: $120,000 revenue and $30,000 owner net at 25%. Base: $560,000 and $196,000 at 35%. Scaled: $1,000,000 and $450,000 at 45%; the scaled scenario uses six people.

stages.label: Principal and relationship lead
stages.detail: Own borrower qualification, lender relationships, engagement terms, concentration reviews, and fee disputes. The owner occupies this operating seat rather than appearing as an uncounted fifth core team member.

stages.label: Credit operations lead
stages.detail: Own application checklists, lender-matrix freshness, submission quality, closing conditions, and CRM accuracy. Use Airtable and HubSpot automation to surface missing documents without automating lender credit decisions.

stages.label: File analysis specialist
stages.detail: Reconcile financial statements, receivables aging, equipment schedules, and borrower debt. Work from restricted assignments and escalate unexplained balance differences before the operations lead releases submissions.

stages.label: Transaction controls specialist
stages.detail: Maintain fee evidence, renewal tracking, access reviews, and exception records. Coordinate outside counsel on licensing or securities questions without representing this contractor as a substitute for required expertise.

stages.label: Additional relationship manager
stages.detail: Expand qualified borrower coverage and lender depth when sustained pipeline demand supports a third full-time seat. Measure funded retained fees and closing quality rather than raw submission volume.

stages.label: Closing and renewal coordinator
stages.detail: Absorb closing-condition follow-up, settlement matching, and renewal scheduling at scaled throughput. Add capacity only after the core pod demonstrates reliable fee collection and bounded exception backlogs.

diagrams.title: Allocate Startup Cash Before Chasing Closings
diagrams.subtitle: Four buckets across $20,000, $60,000, and $100,000 launch budgets.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values are middle-budget USD components and sum to $60,000. Each stage's value and detail also specify lean and upper-budget components; those columns sum to $20,000 and $100,000. These are capital plans, not revenue scenarios. Launch spending and reserve balances must not be counted twice.
diagrams.caption: The middle plan allocates $12,000 + $8,000 + $10,000 + $30,000 = $60,000. A reserve cannot erase the 3–9 month first-deal interval or fund unlimited failed-closing work.

stages.label: Licensing and professional setup
stages.detail: Fund jurisdiction-specific licensing analysis, filings where required, engagement drafting, insurance setup, and compensation review. Restrict launch geography when available capital cannot support the required scope.

stages.label: Secure operating infrastructure
stages.detail: Configure HubSpot, Airtable, Microsoft 365, secure document access, MFA, and backup procedures. Distinguish implementation spending and prepaid subscriptions from later monthly operating expenses.

stages.label: Lender and referral development
stages.detail: Build lender coverage, attend targeted industry events, and develop borrower education materials. Validate permitted referral arrangements before paying anyone for financing introductions or transaction outcomes.

stages.label: Uncommitted operating reserve
stages.detail: Preserve cash for collection delays and failed files. The middle reserve covers 7.5 months at $4,000 monthly cash burn but only 1.67 months at $18,000; nine months at $18,000 requires $162,000 before setup costs.

diagrams.title: Thirty Days to an Evidence-Ready Brokerage Desk
diagrams.subtitle: Build scope, systems, lender fit, and pipeline discipline before forecasting fees.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Four milestones cover Days 1–30 inclusively. Numeric values are milestone end days. This sprint prepares operations; the canonical first-deal expectation remains 3–9 months. Any unresolved licensing requirement prevents affected live activity.
diagrams.caption: Finish the month with a functioning lender matrix, tested application checklist, renewal fields, and a funded runway plan rather than an invented first-month closing target.

stages.label: Define the permitted desk
stages.detail: Choose two initial financing products and launch jurisdictions. Document licensing and fee requirements, assign the four core seats, and reconcile the $120,000, $560,000, and $1,000,000 retained-fee scenarios to their respective margins and team sizes.

stages.label: Build the evidence system
stages.detail: Configure HubSpot stages, Airtable lender fields, document permissions, MFA, and missing-file reminders. Test three synthetic borrower files covering equipment, receivables, and bridge use cases; resolve access and arithmetic defects before loading live records.

stages.label: Validate lender fit
stages.detail: Research eight candidate lenders and obtain documented appetite confirmation from at least four. Record ticket size, geography, collateral, exclusions, fee terms, clawbacks, and contacts. Keep unconfirmed lenders outside automated matching recommendations.

stages.label: Run the controlled pipeline
stages.detail: After required permissions are in place, conduct ten qualified referral conversations and request three complete borrower packages. Treat these as activity targets, not promised conversions. Review cash runway, concentration, file defects, and next-month ownership.
